solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I'm feeling sorry for wordplay in cryptic not comic setting

indicators.note: the pun is placed in the middle of the rearranged letters, the setting that holds it
cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters of not and comic are jumbled

parts.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay

explanation.surface: A setter apologises for slipping a pun into a cryptic puzzle where a comic one might be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' is the anagram signal, not a description of the puzzle, and 'setting' joins 'in' as the container signal. 'I'm' and 'for' are the setter's playful apology framing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Compunction is a pang of guilt or regret, the state of being contrite about something done.

clue.text: Novelist and film-maker combined operations with a cute disposition

parts.note: CO is the military abbreviation for Combined Operations

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of a cute are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A writer-director who teamed up projects with a charming, cute temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament but signals rearranging A CUTE into CTEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Cocteau was a French writer of novels and plays who also directed films such as La Belle et la Bête.

clue.text: Molybdenum covers both hands holding a grinder

parts.note: Mo is the chemical symbol for molybdenum, and in a down clue it covers, sitting on top of, the rest

indicators.note: the two hand letters hold the a between them

parts.note: L and R, for left and right hands

explanation.surface: A metal casing wrapped round two hands gripping a grinding machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back tooth whose broad surface grinds food, so it is a grinder.

clue.text: What made others in Suez die?

definitions.text: What made others in Suez die?

indicators.note: taking every other letter in the words Suez die, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A question about the weapon that killed people in the Suez conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others in' picks the second, fourth and sixth letters of SUEZ DIE. The whole clue also describes the gun, which was used in Middle East fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israeli submachine gun is a weapon that killed many in Middle Eastern wars.

clue.text: Sea-urchins' core feature

indicators.note: the letters sit within the body of the word, at its core

explanation.surface: The central characteristic of sea urchins.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is one of the features of the face, alongside nose and mouth.

clue.text: Unaware Italian gentleman has no need of Southern worker

indicators.note: the gentleman does without the letter for Southern, so it is dropped

parts.note: signor is the Italian title for a gentleman
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman can do without a worker from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, being in the dark about something.

clue.text: Facing cuts before putting on new face

indicators.note: the new letter is put on in front of the rest
the facing letter cuts into the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
V, for versus, means against or facing

explanation.surface: A facing material is cut beforehand, ready to be given a new front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' looks like the definition but gives V (versus); the definition is the final 'face', in the sense of cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the face to do something is to have the cheek or audacity, the same as having the nerve.

clue.text: One who mooches will be no good in prose composition

indicators.note: the no good letters go in the middle of the rearranged prose
a composition puts parts together in a new order, so the letters of prose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cadger would be useless at writing prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like writing but signals the rearrangement, giving SPOER around the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off others, cadging favours, which is what mooching means.

clue.text: Commercial college in Cambridge Time editor owned

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on television
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A college advertisement in a Cambridge magazine that an editor owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge' points to England, but the college is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess it, so owned here means confessed.

clue.text: Brush sheepdogs with one leg but no energy

indicators.note: the sheepdogs come without the energy letter, so it is removed

parts.note: collies are the classic sheepdog breed
E is the physics symbol for energy
I is the Roman numeral one
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Grooming sheepdogs, one of them lame and tired out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' looks like grooming, but means a minor clash. ON is the leg side, the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush is a slight encounter or clash, as in a brush with the law, so it is a crash or clash.

clue.text: Riders' exhibition and what they did with 23 finally

parts.note: riders rode, so this is the past tense of what riders do

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the answer to clue 23

parts.note: clue 23 is the rope for throwing

explanation.surface: A show of riders, and what they did with their ropes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public display of cowboy riding and roping skills.

clue.text: Historic ball game, holding another over, precedes Physical Education: Union in popular parlance?

indicators.note: the first part goes before Physical Education
the first game holds the second inside it

parts.note: E O was an eighteenth-century gambling game where a ball fell into slots marked E or O

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: another ball game, here rugby union, RU

explanation.surface: An old ball game with another game inside it, played before a school sports lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: EO is an obscure eighteenth-century casino game, a forerunner of roulette. In Britain the European Union is often just called Europe in everyday talk, which is why the definition ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the European Union is commonly referred to by the continent's name, so the political union is popularly called this.

clue.text: Bag a prize

definitions.meaning: a handbag or small bag for money
the money awarded to a winner, as in a boxing match

explanation.definitionFit: A purse is both a small money bag and the prize money put up for a contest.

clue.text: Giving information involving cheese and fruit's nitrogen content

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the nitrogen is the fruit's content, placed inside it

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Nutritional information about a cheese and fruit platter's nitrogen levels.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefing is the act of supplying someone with the facts they need.

clue.text: Retroverted uterus nurse regarded as somewhat precarious

indicators.note: retroverted means turned backwards, so the letters read in reverse
somewhat means only part of the words are used

explanation.surface: A nurse considers a tilted womb a somewhat risky condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retroverted' is a real medical term for a tilted uterus but here it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsure can mean insecure or unsteady, as in an unsure footing, hence precarious.

clue.text: Lecturer rolling cigar gets you and me up, to be precise

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: us means you and me

indicators.note: rolling turns the letters of cigar over into a new order

explanation.surface: A lecturer rolling a cigar gets the two of us up to be exact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' gives RGICA and 'up' turns the pronoun so it reads SU; the lecturer's letter comes last though named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical, as in surgical precision, describes something done with great exactness.

clue.text: Is not Revelation 1-3 about angel?

indicators.note: about means round about, so the letters are turned around into a new order
letters one to three of the word Revelation are used, as a Bible verse reference would look

explanation.surface: A question asking whether the opening verses of Revelation concern an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: '1-3' takes the first three letters of Revelation, REV, mimicking a Bible verse reference. 'angel' looks biblical but means a backer of shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who puts money into a theatre production, a kind of financial supporter.

clue.text: Supply one-liner using network?

parts.note: E as in e-mail means electronic, using the computer network
a quip is a witty one-liner

explanation.surface: Sending a one-liner over the internet, like an electronic joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish with what is needed, so to provide or supply.

clue.text: Fit Scots put Queen Victoria up in western isle

indicators.note: the queen's letters go in the island's name

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off the west of Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: VIR stands for Victoria Imperatrix Regina, her title as empress and queen

explanation.surface: Fit Scots placing Queen Victoria on a western island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like healthy but is a noun for a fit of temper; the word is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirrivee is a Scottish word for a fit of temper or tantrum.

clue.text: Powder for the first curries cooked for son getting married

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word the
cooked means prepared or altered, so these letters are mixed up
the son letter gets the married letter in its place

explanation.surface: A spice powder for the first curries, prepared for a son's wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the S of CURRIES for M, add T from 'the first', and 'cooked' rearranges all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow spice ground to a powder from a root, used in curries.

clue.text: Gaoler's name in film that flopped in US

indicators.note: the name letter goes in the middle of the flop

parts.note: turkey is American slang for a flop of a film

explanation.surface: A prison guard's name appears in an American box-office failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a jailer, the one who holds the keys.

clue.text: Returning knight had placed statue in temple

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: to dub someone is to knight them

indicators.note: placed means set in position, so the letters of had are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A returning knight had installed a statue in a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' is a verb here, DUB, read backwards as BUD; 'placed' rearranges HAD into DHA.
explanation.definitionFit: An image of the founder of Buddhism is the statue found in a Buddhist temple.

clue.text: Worm if old and lined wriggles

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if

indicators.note: wriggles suggests movement, so the letters of lined twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A worm that is aged and wrinkled squirms about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' attaches to 'if': AN is the old word for 'if'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annelid is a segmented worm, such as an earthworm or leech.

clue.text: Playful satire about Republican I really roasted

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are wrapped about the Republican letter
roasted means cooked through, so the letters are transformed

explanation.surface: Mocking satire about a Republican who really got a roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or banter.

clue.text: Rope for throwing. Hopalong Cassidy almost might be chap doing it

indicators.note: might be signals that the trimmed name is a jumble of chap doing together with the answer
almost means the name is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Hopalong Cassidy, the film cowboy, might be the chap throwing such a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: HOPALONGCASSID (the name less its last letter, by 'almost') rearranges into CHAP DOING plus 'it', the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope thrown to catch cattle.

clue.text: Firin' lots of bullets? Take year out for injury

indicators.note: take together with out means remove a letter
out with take tells us something is removed

parts.note: sprayin' is firing a hail of bullets, with the final letter dropped as in the clue

explanation.surface: A cowboy firing off bullets takes a year off for an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is an injury to a ligament, as in a twisted ankle.

clue.text: In opening in Adelaide — and Melbourne and Sydney — is batsman out of order?

indicators.note: the word is goes in among the opening letters
the opening letter in each of the three city names

explanation.surface: An Ashes question about a batsman's dismissal at Australian Test grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Adelaide, Melbourne and Sydney are Australian Test cricket venues. 'batsman' is a nod to Dennis Amiss, the England opener, an extra hint to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or faulty, as in something being out of order.

clue.text: American Democrat having circled earth is not fresh

indicators.note: the Democrat has gone round the earth and ended up after it

explanation.surface: An American Democrat who has flown round the world is no longer fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are second-hand, which is to say no longer new.

clue.text: Takes out second-hand Homer reader

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of takes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking out a used copy for someone who reads Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's 'On First Looking into Chapman's Homer' describes reading Homer in translation, so second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats read Homer only in George Chapman's English translation, as his famous sonnet relates.

clue.text: Roman virgin once going round Italy with American soldier is not completely developed

indicators.note: the virgin's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: a Vestal was a virgin priestess of ancient Rome
I is the international code for Italy
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A Roman priestess touring Italy with an American soldier is not fully grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestigial organ is a rudimentary one, never fully formed or no longer functional.

clue.text: Reserve victims for farmer's wife? Presumably not

indicators.note: the farmer's wife cut off tails, presumably not heads, yet here the head goes

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the tails of three blind mice

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme joke questioning whether the farmer's wife had mice in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Three Blind Mice' the farmer's wife cuts off their tails; the clue jokes that she did not cut off heads, but the head M is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice means coolness of manner, which is the same as reserve or aloofness.

clue.text: Odder verses in revue (given audience's perception) may be too saucy

indicators.note: heard by an audience, in revue sounds like in review, and a review revises, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange verses sung in a revue might strike the audience as risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revue (given audience's perception)' asks you to hear 'in review', the anagram signal. 'saucy' suggests risqué, but means having too much dressing, as a salad might.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad with too much dressing has been given too much sauce, a pun on saucy.
